THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Split Plate Mediterranean Snack Box

Mediterranean-inspired kid snack box — prosciutto, Babybel, Castelvetrano olives, and almond-flour crackers. 4 boxes at once for 2 kids across 2 days. About 270 cal / 16g protein per box.

YIELD4 servings
TOTAL TIME5 min active — no cook
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~270 cal | ~16g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: Drain the olives WELL before boxing. Wet olives soak into prosciutto + crackers = compartment cross-contamination.

Ingredients

PER BOX (yields 1 snack box)

  • 2 oz Del Duca prosciutto (or any prosciutto with comparable macros)
  • 1 Original Babybel cheese
  • 1.5 label servings Castelvetrano olives (drained well)
  • 0.5 label serving Simple Mills Fine Ground Sea Salt almond-flour crackers

FOUR-BOX BATCH (recommended)

  • 8 oz prosciutto total
  • 4 Original Babybel cheeses
  • 6 label servings Castelvetrano olives
  • 2 label servings Simple Mills almond-flour crackers

You want a no-cook 4-box batch that lasts 2 kids × 2 days. Also useful when introducing kids to less-familiar foods — the kid-participation moment (letting them place olives + crackers) turns exposure into low-pressure play. Ep. 5 of the Split Plate Snack Box series.

Method

  1. 1.SET UP. Set out four divided snack boxes (4-compartment Bento-style — same format as Snack Box Series Ep. 1-4).
  2. 2.PROSCIUTTO. Fold 2 oz prosciutto LOOSELY into one compartment of each box. Loose folds hold up better than tight rolls (less compression, more visual air).
  3. 3.BABYBEL. Drop one wrapped Original Babybel into the cheese compartment of each box. Keep the wax on — kids open their own, and the wax-peel ritual is part of the appeal.
  4. 4.OLIVES. Drain the Castelvetrano olives WELL (wet olives soak into other compartments). Divide 1.5 servings into the olive compartment of each box. FOR KIDS UNDER 4 — quarter lengthwise (see notes). Over 4 with good chewing = whole is fine but supervise.
  5. 5.CRACKERS. Add 0.5 serving Simple Mills almond-flour crackers to the DRY compartment of each box. Keep them dry — moisture from olives / prosciutto softens them.
  6. 6.KIDS HELP BUILD (optional but recommended). Let kids place the olives + crackers themselves. Turns exposure into low-pressure play. Doesn't guarantee they'll eat — just makes the food feel less unfamiliar.
  7. 7.LID + CHILL. Snap lid on each box. Refrigerate — prosciutto + cheese need it. For lunchboxes, pack with an ice pack. Serve chilled.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid: Serve the kid portion as described above.

Keys to success

  • Keep the cracker compartment DRY. Add crackers shortly before serving OR seal the lid tightly so olive brine + prosciutto moisture stay put.
  • Loose prosciutto folds > tight rolls. Loose = better visual + easier to grab. Tight = compressed + harder to pull out.

Storage and reheating

Store: Assemble the 4 boxes in one 5-minute pass. Refrigerate immediately — prosciutto + Babybel need it. Best within 2 days.

Reheat: Don't — serve chilled. Prosciutto reads best cold; Babybel firms up in the fridge.

Lasts: 2 days max in the fridge. Crackers soften after 24 hours even in the sealed compartment — add them shortly before serving if packing more than a day ahead.

Estimated nutrition

~270 cal | ~16g protein.

About 270 cal / 16g protein per snack box, user-approved headline. Component breakdown (per box): 2 oz Del Duca prosciutto (~70 cal / 9g protein) + 1 Babybel Original (~70 cal / 5g protein) + 1.5 servings Castelvetrano olives (~45 cal / 0g protein) + 0.5 serving Simple Mills almond crackers (~75 cal / 1.5g protein). Total: ~260 cal / ~15.5g protein raw component sum. Rounded to the user-approved 270 / 16 headline as a practical allowance for brand + portion variation. Do not describe as laboratory-verified.

Adult plate

Adult

Adult-friendly batch too — steal a box from the meal-prep stack. Prosciutto + olives + Babybel hits an adult snack cleanly at ~270 cal / 16g protein.

Kid plate

Kid

SAFETY: Castelvetrano olives are round + slippery. Under 4 = quarter lengthwise. Over 4 with good chewing = whole is fine but supervise the first few bites. Per CDC choking-hazard guidance for spherical foods. Also: kids helping place the olives + crackers turns unfamiliar-food exposure into low-pressure play — but don't oversell the trick (helping doesn't guarantee eating).

Three keys to success

  1. 1Drain the olives WELL before boxing. Wet olives soak into prosciutto + crackers = compartment cross-contamination.
  2. 2Keep the cracker compartment DRY. Add crackers shortly before serving OR seal the lid tightly so olive brine + prosciutto moisture stay put.
  3. 3Loose prosciutto folds > tight rolls. Loose = better visual + easier to grab. Tight = compressed + harder to pull out.

Brands I use

Del Duca
Prosciutto (~70 cal / 9g protein per 2 oz).
The protein anchor — 9g per box, over half the total protein target. Del Duca is the shown label; any prosciutto with comparable macros works (Boar's Head, Volpi, Fratelli Beretta). Sub any dry-cured Italian ham that fits the 2 oz / 70 cal window.
Babybel
Original semisoft cheese wedge (~70 cal / 5g protein / 6g fat per wedge).
Kid-proof cheese unit — same brand as Snack Box Series Ep. 3 (Berry Power-Up). Individually wrapped in wax, no cutting or portioning, ~5g protein per wedge. Kids open their own; the wax-peel ritual is part of the appeal.
Castelvetrano Olives
Buttery green Sicilian olives, pitted (~15 cal per olive; 1.5 servings ≈ 45 cal per box).
The Mediterranean identity + the food-exposure moment. Castelvetrano's buttery flavor + bright green color reads friendly (less intense than Kalamata). Look for pitted; whole with pits = choking risk for kids. Quarter lengthwise for under 4s per CDC.
Simple Mills
Fine Ground Sea Salt almond-flour crackers (~150 cal / 3g protein per full serving; half-serving per box ≈ 75 cal).
The crunch signal + gluten-free option. Almond flour base = tree nut allergen (do NOT call school-safe). Cross-recipe candidate for any snack box that wants a crunchy cracker without wheat.
